_publication.note: Published copy for documentation. Sanitized on 2026-09-25 PT: local file paths, cache paths, account names and people's names were removed or generalized; the question text, closed sets, thresholds and fail-closed rules are unchanged. This contract embeds NO real posts, X post text, author handles, term example posts, holdout ids or database contents: the {term}/{pid}/STATE fields are template placeholders filled at run time. The illustrative state under 'synthetic_example' (where present) is invented and clearly synthetic.

provenance: NEW 2026-09-25 11:24 PT, rebuilt-series label (not an original contract). External dictionary attestation (Urban Dictionary, Green's, Wiktionary): an entry whose sense matches the term's slang-sense meaning satisfies path C's '>= 2 explainers' part only (path label attested_dictionary); only the matching sense counts. Jev only judges whether each dictionary sense matches the corpus usage. General instructions; no term-specific hints.

urbandictionary.note: exact-word entries in API order; the API currently returns 0 votes for every entry, so no vote floor is possible (user-generated: weakest source)

wiktionary.note: English-section definition lines with their {{lb}} labels; quotation lines (##*) skipped

greens.note: exact-headword search results, then the entry page's definition text

fetch: Crawl4AI (self-hosted, free); no Firecrawl, no X. Fetched pages are cached permanently, so a term is fetched only the first time it is looked up.

question.instructions: STATE.dictionary_senses['{d}'] is one dictionary sense (source: {src}) of '{term}'. STATE.posts show how '{term}' is used as slang in our corpus; STATE.meaning, if not empty, is its recorded slang meaning. Does this dictionary sense describe the SAME slang sense as that corpus usage (a close paraphrase, or a broader or narrower wording of the same sense, counts)? A different sense of the same spelling (literal, older, unrelated, or a different slang meaning) is DIFFERENT.

criteria.MATCH: the dictionary sense is the same slang sense as the corpus usage
criteria.DIFFERENT: a different sense of the same spelling, or unrelated

statuses.NO_SLANG_POSTS: no slang-sense posts to compare against (not attested)

fail_closed: fetch error with no match found, or Jev error: no row is written for the term (previous row kept); the export fails that term closed.
